---
title: "The Properties of Meaning as Geometry"
---

This chapter is a stub. Its outline follows the roadmap in [index.qmd](../index.qmd) and exists so that later chapters can already cross-reference its sections. It is a catalog: each section states one property that meaning acquires once it becomes position in a space, in the plain language of distance and direction, and points forward to the chapters that earn it.

## Nearness Is Likeness {#sec-prop-nearness}
*Things that mean alike sit close together, and things that mean differently sit far apart.*

Figure (planned): a small map in which "dog", "puppy", and "wolf" cluster, while "car" and "doorbell" sit far away.

Earned in Chapter 3 (where the distances come from), Chapter 2 (why distance still works in many dimensions), and Chapter 4 (search by nearness).

## Difference Is a Relation {#sec-prop-difference}
*The step from one meaning to another is itself meaningful, and the same step can be taken from elsewhere.*

Figure (planned): the analogy parallelogram, with the step from "man" to "woman" repeated from "king" to "queen".

Earned in Chapter 3 (analogy), Chapter 7 (relations as translations and rotations), and Chapter 12 (aligning two spaces by their steps rather than their points).

## A Direction Is a Meaning You Can Move Along {#sec-prop-direction}
*Some directions carry a single quality, such as plural, past, or formal, and moving along them changes only that quality.*

Figure (planned): a sentence nudged along one direction, changing tone while keeping its topic.

Earned in Chapter 3 (directions as concepts, steering), Chapter 5 (features as directions), and Chapter 2 (why there is room for so many directions).

## Meaning Can Be a Region {#sec-prop-region}
*A concept is not always a point: it can be an area, a cone, or a subspace, and one concept can contain another.*

Figure (planned): "dog" as a region inside "animal", with the individual dogs as points within it.

Earned in Chapter 6 (hierarchies in curved space) and Chapter 9 (concepts as subspaces).

## Meaning Can Move: Paths {#sec-prop-paths}
*A static thing is a point, and an event, a plan, or an argument is a path through the space.*

Figure (planned): a running dog drawn as a curve, each frame a point along it.

Earned in Chapter 6 (geodesics and trajectories) and Chapter 13 (motion, time, and planning in the space).

Note on reasoning. A model's chain of thought is such a path, but one that keeps collapsing back to words: at every step the position in the space is rounded to a token and then read back in. It sits on Shannon's boundary, the reasoning version of the split between bits and meaning (Chapter 3, "Shannon's Boundary Problem"). Whether reasoning can stay in the space instead of passing through text is an open question, developed in Chapter 5, Chapter 13, and the Epilogue.

## Meanings Combine {#sec-prop-combine}
*Two meanings can be added into a bundle or bound into a pair, and the result is again a position in the same space.*

Figure (planned): "red" and "ball" combined into "red ball", and the failure case where "red ball, blue cube" cannot say which colour belongs to which object.

Earned in Chapter 10 (bundling and binding) and Chapter 11 (composition and systematicity).

## Many Senses, One Space {#sec-prop-senses}
*A photograph, a word, a bark, and a gait of the same dog can land near each other, and far from a cat or a car.*

Figure (planned): the four signals of the dog test of the Prologue, converging on one neighbourhood.

Earned in Chapter 13 (multimodal embeddings) and Chapter 12 (aligning separate spaces).

## What Is Real Is the Arrangement {#sec-prop-arrangement}
*The coordinates mean nothing on their own; only the distances and directions between meanings carry information, so the whole space can be turned without changing what it says.*

Figure (planned): the same map rotated, with every distance and every analogy preserved.

Earned in Chapter 3 (invariance to relabelling), Chapter 8 (the shape of a representation), and Chapter 12 (comparing two spaces up to a rotation).
